subject: Mosaic Finance — Infosec scorecard & action plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mosaicfinance.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@mosaicfinance.com>, security@mosaicfinance.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Mosaic Finance — quick recap and infosec scorecard (next steps)

Tom / Amy / Infosec team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid conversation. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, and the concrete asks we agreed on so we all have alignment going into intake/contracting.

Call attendees: Tom Ellis (Mosaic Finance), Amy Chen (Mosaic Finance), Monica Patel (Redwood), Rishi Malhotra (Redwood, joined briefly), Laura Bennett (Redwood, invited)

Key pain points / goals (as stated by Mosaic):
- Regulated payments workload: need predictable auditability for transactions and user events across production and retained artifacts.
- Evidence for procurement: SOC 2 Type II report and AOC, recent pen-test summary (redacted), and an artifact list mapped to controls.
- Audit logs: need schema/export (JSONL preferred), retention policy, and proof of immutability/chain of custody for logs used in investigations.
- Data residency & DPA: default hosting in US but some contracts require specific DPA language and subprocessor disclosure.

What Redwood committed / proposed during the call:
- Provide our latest SOC 2 AOC + a mapping document showing which Redwood controls map to Mosaic’s procurement checklist.
- Share a redacted pen-test summary and the vulnerability remediation cadence.
- Deliver a sample audit-log export (JSON Lines) showing schema and available fields, plus options for archival retention (S3 export, cold storage).
- Share a DPA draft and confirm standard subprocessor list; we can accommodate an extended retention option via Dedicated/Private deployments if required.

Immediate asks / next steps (owner / ETA):
- Monica: send scorecard + DPA draft (attached) — DONE (see attachments).
- Mosaic: confirm whether 2-year retention is sufficient or if your regulators expect longer (Tom / Amy) — please reply.
- Rishi (cc): take lead on SOC 2 artifacts + audit-log sample; target to deliver initial artifacts by 2026-09-15.
- Legal / Procurement (Mosaic): redline DPA by 2026-09-22 so we can scope contract changes.
- Follow-up call: propose Wed 2026-09-16, 10:00am ET to walk artifacts and answer technical Qs.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-infosec-scorecard.xlsx (scorecard mapping template)
- DPA-draft.pdf (Redwood standard DPA draft)
- audit-log-sample.jsonl (sample, redacted events)

Open questions we need from Mosaic to finalize scope:
1) Required retention window (2 years vs. 7 years vs. other)
2) Any contractual language outside our standard DPA (e.g., specific audit rights or TLS/HSM requirements)
3) Desired timing for legal review + expected procurement checklist deadline

If you can reply inline on the three open questions that will let Rishi and I prioritize artifacts. Happy to hop on the 9/16 slot — please confirm.

Best,

Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

--

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mosaicfinance.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 18:02:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Mosaic Finance — quick recap and infosec scorecard (next steps)

Thanks Monica — useful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachments: 

1) Retention: our initial procurement asks for 2 years, but compliance has flagged a potential requirement for 7 years for certain transaction metadata. We'll confirm on Monday but please plan for the possibility of longer-term archival (S3/archive).

2) SOC 2 / AOC: we need the most recent AOC (Type II) and a control mapping into our questionnaire. Can you confirm date of last audit and whether the auditor will provide an AOC?

3) Pen test: we expect a redacted summary with scope and remediation timeline. Will Redwood share the last external pentest report summary (redacted) and the most recent patching cadence?

4) Audit logs: JSONL export is our preference. Can Redwood provide both the raw events schema and an option to push daily rollups to our S3 bucket? Also need retention & immutability options (WORM or signed logs) called out.

5) Data residency / key management: we use customer-managed keys in some vendors. Do you support HSM/KMS integrations and can Redwood sign an attestation around key separation?

We can do Wed 9/16 10:00am ET — tentatively confirmed. If you can have Rishi on the call that'd be great. I've attached a short Q/A doc with two items specific to audit log sampling.

Tom Ellis
Head of Security Engineering | Mosaic Finance
Tom.Ellis@mosaicfinance.com | +1 212-555-0987

Monica / Laura,

Thanks — happy to own the technical artifacts and coordinate with Security/IR. Quick replies inline to Mosaic's asks and the internal checklist: 

SOC 2 / AOC:
- Our most recent Type II audit completed Nov 2025; we have the AOC and the full report available. I'll produce a control-mapping sheet that maps Redwood controls to Mosaic's procurement questions. ETA: produce AOC + mapping by 2026-09-15.

Pen test:
- We can provide a redacted external pen-test summary (scope, high-severity findings, remediation status). The full report is restricted but we will provide the summary and timelines. ETA: 2026-09-18.

Audit logs & retention:
- Export format: Redwood can export raw events as JSONL (schema attached in sample). Fields include timestamp, request_id, model_id, user_id (redacted), action, response_token_count, ip_origin, and outcome_code.
- Delivery options: push to customer S3 (daily), or we can provide S3 lifecycle rules for cold archival. Default hosted retention is 90 days; Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured to retain up to multi-year via archival exports.
- Immutability: we offer signed log bundles and S3 object-lock (WORM) for Dedicated customers; for hosted we can provide signed daily manifests and third-party notarization on request.
- I'll attach an audit-log-sample.jsonl and a short schema doc. ETA: 2026-09-15.

KMS / HSM:
- We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS with limited HSM attestation; we can provide an attestation letter and a subprocessor list to satisfy procurement.

DPA / legal:
- Laura, please review Mosaic's redline when it arrives; I'll support technical call responses.

Proposed artifact delivery dates (per internal plan):
- 2026-09-15: SOC 2 AOC + control mapping, audit-log sample.jsonl
- 2026-09-18: redacted pen-test summary and remediation cadence
- 2026-09-22: DPA response and commercial commentary (Laura)

I'll be on the 2026-09-16 call (10:00am ET) and will bring the audit-log sample and mapping to walk through. If Mosaic confirms the 7-year retention need we'll scope an S3 + lifecycle/WORM design and provide rough cost delta at the call.

Action owners: Rishi (artifacts), Laura (DPA/legal), Monica (customer coordination / scheduling)

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
